# Strong fixture draft (fixture-only synthetic)

## Introduction

This report argues that Inditex can turn a sustainability target into a defensible advantage only where the target, the buying decision, and the audit agree, and it tests that claim against a downturn.

## Drivers of sustainability-centric SCM

Regulation binds the chain, and buyer expectations set the timetable. Lloyd's List reporting on carrier fuel rules shows the regulatory edge is external to the firm, which is why Inditex cannot meet the driver alone.

## Benefits of integrating sustainability

The benefit is not the headline saving but the lower variance in a supplier's water and energy use, which shows up as a steadier cost per garment. A Statista series on Spanish textile imports is used to size the exposure rather than to praise the firm.

## Integration to competitive advantage

The judgement is that the advantage sits in the audited tier, and that the audit's scope is the limit. Inditex's tier-one audit covers fabric but not shipping, so the claim is strong where the audit reaches and weak where it does not. This is the reading the 30% weight asks for.

## Recession relevance

A downturn shortens order runs, and the chain's fixed cost then dominates. Because the audited tier has the measure, the shorter run is cheaper there, so the advantage survives the recession without a second claim.

## Conclusion

The report's line holds inside the audit and fails outside it, and the recession is the test that makes the limit visible.
